transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-28 15:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Evan Brooks (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Dana Liu (PicoMed CTO), Marcus Green (SRE), Sofia Ortiz (Product)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): walkthrough of Console request debugging features; agreed to run request playback and share security package.

[00:00] Evan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Evan from Redwood, AE on the account. Priya will be walking through the console traces — she owns the SE side. Dana, Marcus, Sofia, thanks for carving time.

[00:12] Dana: Thanks Evan. Quick note — Marcus is the one who will be looking at the SRE level stuff; I'm more product/arch. We have been seeing sporadic spikes in latency and a couple 5xxs last week.

[00:22] Marcus: Yeah, the 95th to 99th percentile jump around peak ingestion, and we suspect either KV cache warmup or some client-side backpressure.

[00:33] Priya: Cool, that's exactly what we'll try to surface today — I want to show request inspector, request playback, and how the KV cache metrics show up next to trace timelines.

[00:45] Evan: Quick calendar check — we have about 45 minutes; I'll let Priya drive. Priya, take it away.

[00:52] Priya: Okay I'm sharing my screen. First screen is the Request Explorer — you can filter by model, route, status, token count. I'm going to search for the failing trace ID Marcus shared earlier, but first I'll show a time slice around last Wednesday 2–4pm.

[01:20] (screen noise, brief pause)

[01:29] Priya: Alright here's a cluster of high-latency requests, you can see the timeline bar and the waterfall. Note the orange sections are backend processing and the purple is token generation time. The waterfall shows a KV cache miss at the 0.7 second mark — that's probably the warmup you mentioned.

[01:55] Marcus: Hmm, that miss shouldn't happen for our pinned model, we pin to the lower-latency variant. Could there be a fallback?

[02:05] Priya: Good question — our routing policy supports model variant fallback. You can click into the request metadata; here's the route policy: 'latency_preferred' with an automatic fallback to cheaper-quantized variant when load is high. I can show the routing trace.

[02:25] (typing)

[02:31] Priya: See here — this specific request shows a fallback event at 02:11:34 UTC to the q4_0 variant, and the KV cache had a cold miss because sequence length prefetch didn't hit.

[02:50] Dana: q4_0 — is that the quantized variant we tested? We worry about quality when we fall back.

[02:58] Priya: Yes q4_0 is a 4-bit quantization variant, lower memory, and sometimes slight quality differences. In the console you can compare outputs side by side for the original and fallback model — I'll open that.

[03:15] (clicks, UI lag)

[03:21] Priya: Here's the side-by-side output diff and a similarity score. For this request the similarity is high, so quality degradation is small, but you can set policies to prefer model continuity over cost.

[03:40] Marcus: Can we disable fallback for the critical route? We need deterministic latency.

[03:46] Evan: Absolutely — you can set a per-route policy in the Console, pin to specific model versions and disable fallbacks. That will increase cost but give predictable tail latency.

[03:58] Sofia: Where do we see the audit logs for who accessed what? For compliance we need request-level retention and SSO-linked identity.

[04:06] Priya: Under Governance -> Audit logs, each request includes the token, the API key owner, and metadata for the route. We integrate with customer KMS and SAML SSO so audit lines include user ids. I'll pull an audit export example.

[04:25] (short pause)

[04:30] Priya: Export shows request_id, timestamp, api_key, route, model, status, latency_ms — you can configure retention. We also push logs to your SIEM via our GCP/AWS connector if you want.

[04:50] Marcus: Good. For the trace we need to capture KV cache hit ratio over time, can the Console overlay that metric?

[04:58] Priya: Yes — in the trace detail view there's a metrics lane. You can add KV cache hit_rate, prefix_hit, and per-shard latency. See these small green dots on the timeline? Those are cache hits.

[05:15] Dana: The timeline has a couple of odd long tail spikes — can you show a raw request playback? I want to see payload and full timings.

[05:23] Priya: Sure — selecting a request and clicking 'Playback' will re-run it in a sandboxed environment with the original payload. Playback captures exact timing and reproduces the same serving path, including cache layers. Note: we mask any PII unless you provide a redacted sample set.

[05:45] Marcus: When you say reproduces, does it hit the live KV cache or a frozen snapshot? We don't want playback to evict live keys.

[05:55] Priya: Good point — playback runs against a snapshot of the serving state by default to avoid side effects. For full end-to-end reproduction we can run in a dedicated staging cluster that mirrors production traffic.

[06:10] Sofia: Can we schedule bulk playback to re-run a day's worth of 500 requests?

[06:15] Priya: Yes, bulk playback is supported — you upload a request bundle and it runs as a job. We'll provide throughput controls so it doesn't overwhelm your checkpoints.

[06:26] Evan: Priya, could you demo a failing 5xx trace and show how we'd triage to code, infra, or model?

[06:33] Priya: Absolutely — pulling up a 5xx now. This one shows a long runtime in the tokenizer step then an OOM in the runtime kernel. The trace shows a kernel exception at 0.9s and a subsequent 502 returned.

[06:50] Marcus: OOM in runtime — that sounds like bad batching or a bad sequence length distribution.

[06:56] Priya: Right — the console shows request-level batch size and max token length. You can see this request had a 5k token payload which triggered a large memory footprint; batch coalescing pushed an extra 1.2x memory cost. We annotate suspected causes and suggest mitigations.

[07:20] (someone coughs)

[07:25] Priya: There's also a 'Suggested fixes' panel — it recommended enabling per-route max_tokens=1024 and switching to a smaller batching window for this route. We can also set automatic fallbacks to smaller-sequence variants to avoid OOM.

[07:43] Dana: Does Redwood alert on these automatically? We want to be notified when a route crosses error thresholds.

[07:49] Priya: Yes, Alerts -> create alert. You pick metric (error rate, latency p95, KV miss rate), threshold, and notification channels (PagerDuty, Slack, email). Alerts can also trigger automated actions like flow fallback or routing to dedicated capacity.

[08:05] Marcus: Can the alerts include the request playback link so SRE can jump straight to the failing request?

[08:10] Priya: They do. The payload includes the request_id and a play button if you have permission. It also includes a condensed trace snippet.

[08:20] (brief typing)

[08:28] Priya: I'm going to open the 'Trace Correlation' view — this is useful when a user reports a symptom and you want correlated requests. You can group by user_id, model, or api_key and see adjacent requests within a time window.

[08:45] Marcus: That's helpful, our issue was an auth library bump that serialized slightly differently so some payloads spiked.

[08:52] Priya: We can show a diff of the tokenization step across two requests. See how token counts changed for the same input? Subtle differences can change downstream memory.

[09:08] Evan: A question from procurement — what of the artifacts we export can be used for audits? Logs, traces, playback outputs?

[09:16] Priya: You can export full audit logs and trace bundles as gzipped JSON. For audits we can provide certificate of data handling and chain of custody. Everything is signed and timestamped if you choose our long-term retention add-on.

[09:32] Dana: On retention — what's the max retention for raw traces? We might need 2 years for regulation.

[09:38] Priya: By default 90 days, but enterprise retention can be extended to multi-year with add-on. We'll send the SLAs for that.

[09:48] Marcus: Back to KV cache — can you show shard-level hot-keys? We saw a handful of keys getting hammered.

[09:55] Priya: Sure, filter by prefix in the Cache Insights tab. You can highlight top keys and export a histogram. The Console also recommends smoothing rules like client-side jitter or rate limiting to avoid hot-key spikes.

[10:12] Sofia: If we enable Dedicated capacity, does that change the trace story? Like private KV stores?

[10:19] Priya: Dedicated gives you isolated GPU pools and optionally dedicated KV backends. It reduces noisy neighbor effects. The Console UI is the same; you'll just see lower variance in latency and more predictable cache behavior.

[10:34] Marcus: Cost question — will pinning to a non-fallback model materially increase cost? Can the Console show cost-vs-latency tradeoffs?

[10:42] Priya: Yes — Cost Analyzer shows token-level unit cost and projected monthly spend for route configs. You can run scenario simulations: pin-to-model vs allow fallback vs batch size tweaks and see estimated delta.

[10:58] Evan: I'm going to share a quick sample sheet we use for the playback — it's basically a small CSV with request_id, payload (redacted), and headers. Marcus, if you can drop a zipped sample into the shared drive, Priya can kick off the bulk playback.

[11:13] Marcus: Will do.

[11:16] (brief pause)

[11:20] Priya: One more feature — 'Auto-sleuth' which runs a set of heuristics on a failing request and auto-suggests likely causes with confidence scores. It's noisy sometimes but a useful first pass. For this account I can enable it on demo so you can see the suggestions.

[11:36] Dana: Let's enable it, we want everything that speeds triage.

[11:40] (screen sharing ends briefly)

[11:50] Evan: Great. Quick recap — Priya will run a 48-hour playback on the sample set and look specifically for KV-cache miss patterns and verify fallback policy behavior; Evan will share security docs and pricing; Marcus will upload example failing requests; Sofia will consolidate pilot criteria. Anything else?

[12:10] Sofia: Could we add a short runbook for on-call? Like a checklist that SREs can follow when they get an alert.

[12:18] Priya: Yes, we have runbook templates — I can share a starter one customized for your routes.

[12:25] Marcus: One more quick Q — for bulk playback is there a cost estimate? Do we get billed for replay tokens?

[12:31] Evan: Playback jobs are metered and billed at a discounted dev rate; we'll include estimates in the follow-up.

[12:38] Dana: Awesome. Thanks, this was helpful and concrete.

[12:43] Evan: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with notes and the security pack. Priya, I'll hand it back to you to close.

[12:50] Priya: Thanks all. I'll send the playback plan and kick things off once Marcus drops the sample set.

[12:57] (meeting ends)

Note: transcript contains occasional mis-transcriptions ("KV cash" heard as "KV cache" etc) and speaker attribution may be fuzzy in a few short segments.
